page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for disk operations. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded performance offset by constrained multi-threaded execution due to its low thread count. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1580.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1857.29, both falling within the median band for cloud instances. However, Geekbench multi-core performance reaches 1851.0, and the overall PassMark CPU score settles at 2932.06, reflecting the lower-tier processing capacity of a two-vCPU footprint. Large-block memory bandwidth yields 15.1 GB/sec read and 13.5 GB/sec write throughput.

Given its balanced resource profile and modest parallel compute capability, ecs.g7.large is tailored for lightweight workloads that do not demand heavy concurrent computation. Appropriate applications include small-scale web serving, light microservices, internal development environments, and low-traffic application hosting.
